correctness.rationale: The unnormalized Laplacian has three nonzero eigenspace types: within-A eigenvalue q, within-B eigenvalue p, and between-part eigenvalue p+q. Their decomposition gives an exact heat edge difference. A Lipschitz constraint and a coefficient split prove the sharp edge dual bound z+2max(u,v), with explicit attaining 0,±1 potentials. Ordering p≤q implies v≥u for every t>0. Differentiation proves all time transitions and peak formula. For p=q=1 and n=2 the separate exponential cases were checked. A standard-library rational checker confirms exact heat matrices and integral-potential optima for 50 size/time cases; a distinct matrix-exponential/LP comparison checks 245 cases. The analytic proof—not finite computation—settles the infinite family.

value.rationale: The graph-Lipschitz/transport seminorm is a natural stability measure of graph heat flow. The exact all-time sharp norm quantifies how degree imbalance produces temporary Lipschitz growth despite maximum-norm Markov contraction; it identifies the unique time and size of the peak, explicit worst-case inputs, and an optimal global factor 2. These quantitative questions are not answered by prior yes/no curvature or edge-total-variation thresholds and form a natural infinite-family benchmark.
